observation.visible_scene: A coastal beach at low sun (dusk or dawn). The sun sits just above a flat horizon, partly veiled by a thick overcast sky, and casts a bright vertical glitter path on the otherwise calm sea. On the right, a dark headland/cliff is topped by a pale multi-windowed building. A sloping sandy shore occupies the lower foreground, with a thin line of wave foam marking the waterline on the right side. The framing of the sun, cliff, building and horizon is identical across all frames, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: The only continuous motion is the gentle wave action at the shoreline: the foam edge near the right of the beach shifts slightly back and forth (a small swash oscillation) and its width/shape changes frame to frame.

A small dark object (rock/debris) that sits at the foam line on the right in the early frames (roughly t=0.0–0.9 s) is no longer visible against the foam in the later frames as the waterline moves; by the end the foam band is narrower and closer to the right edge.
The sun's reflection column on the water continuously changes in texture as surface ripples pass through it; the open-sea surface shows subtle, ongoing ripple motion.
The sky, cloud pattern, sun position, cliff silhouette and building remain fixed throughout the excerpt (no camera pan/zoom, no change in exposure).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the dark object is a permanent rock that stays on the beach (only temporarily covered by foam) or something that has moved out of the foam area cannot be determined from this segment.
The longer-term trend of the tide/wave set-up or set-down is unknown because both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
uncertain_details: The exact direction of the foam-line shift is hard to pin down; it oscillates by a small amount rather than translating cleanly, so it is best described as a back-and-forth swash.
The identity of the dark object at the waterline (rock vs. shadow vs. debris) is not certain.
